title: Typed-DSL Constrained Data Recipes for Higher Executability in DataChef

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to identify why DataChef's free-form Python data recipes fail to execute successfully, focusing on categorizing failure modes. No prior paper explicitly identifies failure causes for free-form Python data recipes or categorizes them into DSL-addressable structural issues versus non-DSL-addressable semantic ones. Papers like [6] and [21] discuss error causes in SQL query formulation and syntax errors in programming, respectively, but neither addresses the specific context of Python data recipes or the DSL categorization framework. Thus, no prior paper establishes the same empirical relationship.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves an automated failure-mode audit on 50 independently sampled recipes per task, categorizing failures into structural (DSL-addressable) and semantic (non-DSL-addressable) issues. Papers [20], [22], and [23] describe general failure mode analysis methodologies, but they do not apply these methods to Python data recipes or use the specific categorization into DSL-addressable versus non-DSL-addressable issues. Paper [25] discusses failure reproduction using LLMs but focuses on debugging rather than categorizing failure modes. Therefore, no prior paper employs a substantively equivalent mechanism.

### Evaluation
The evaluation reports the proportion of failures that are structural and DSL-addressable (45-61%) and the contribution of syntax errors (13-17%). Papers [5], [14], and [16] evaluate LLM-generated code for syntax and logic errors, constraints, and security risks, respectively, using benchmarks and metrics. These papers use similar evaluation designs (e.g., measuring error rates and categorizing errors) applied to different objects (e.g., general-purpose code or DSLs). Thus, the evaluation design is covered.

### Domain
The domain is automated data engineering and LLM data recipe generation. Papers [8], [9], [10], and [15] address LLM-based code generation for DSLs and domain-specific programming tasks, which fall within the same general application area. Although the specific focus on Python data recipes is new, the broader domain of LLM-driven DSL code generation is covered.
